news.headline: Brookline starts Perimeter at buy; PT C$1.54
news.summary: Brookline Capital Markets initiated research coverage on Perimeter Medical Imaging AI with a Buy rating and a C$1.54 (US$1.11) price target, citing Claire's FDA Breakthrough Device status and the company's pending CMS New Technology APC reimbursement filing, with a decision expected by year-end 2026. The stock had closed at C$0.32 on July 13, 2026 ahead of the initiation.

news.headline: Paradigm Capital names Perimeter and maintains Profound as healthcare Top Picks
news.summary: Paradigm Capital analyst Scott McAuley added Perimeter Medical Imaging AI to the firm's list of top healthcare picks alongside Profound Medical, reiterating a Speculative Buy rating with a roughly C$0.95 price target. The pick reflects growing analyst attention on Perimeter following Claire's FDA approval and the pending Medicare reimbursement pathway.

news.headline: Perimeter Selected for INOVAIT Pilot Fund to Advance AI for Breast Cancer Surgery
news.summary: Perimeter Medical Imaging AI was selected to receive up to nearly $148,000 in contributions from the INOVAIT Pilot Fund to help build more robust, scalable AI capabilities for its flagship Claire imaging device. The funding supports continued development of the AI-enabled OCT platform used for real-time breast cancer surgical margin assessment.

news.headline: Perimeter Medical Imaging AI Closes Final Tranche of Non-Brokered Private Placement
news.summary: Perimeter closed the second and final tranche of its non-brokered private placement of convertible debentures, issuing CDN$3,280,000 in principal and bringing aggregate proceeds from the two-tranche offering to CDN$6,040,000 (including CDN$2,760,000 taken up by CEO Adrian Mendes in the first tranche). The debenture financing followed the company's earlier LIFE Offering and adds to cash reserves supporting continued commercialization of Claire and the S-Series OCT platform.

catalysts.label: CMS New Technology APC decision for Claire OCT
catalysts.detail: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services is expected to rule on Perimeter's New Technology Ambulatory Payment Classification (NT-APC) filing for Claire under the Medicare Outpatient Prospective Payment System; Claire's FDA Breakthrough Device status is expected to expedite the review.

catalysts.label: Potential NT-APC reimbursement effective date
catalysts.detail: If CMS grants New Technology APC status following the company's June 2026 filing cycle, incremental Medicare reimbursement for Claire procedures would take effect around January 1, 2027 and remain in place for roughly 2-3 years while claims data is collected ahead of reassignment to a standard APC.

catalysts.label: Second quarter 2026 financial results
catalysts.detail: Perimeter is expected to report Q2 2026 (period ended June 30, 2026) financial and operating results; based on the Q1 2026 reporting cadence (results issued May 28, 2026), no official Q2 date had been announced as of August 5, 2026.

pulse: Perimeter Medical Imaging AI continues commercializing Claire, the first FDA-approved AI-enabled OCT imaging device for real-time intraoperative breast cancer margin assessment, while expanding its base of S-Series OCT hospital placements; June 2026 brought an INOVAIT pilot grant (up to ~$148,000) to advance Claire's AI capabilities and the close of a CDN$6.04 million convertible debenture financing (heavily backed by CEO Adrian Mendes), extending the company's cash runway. Analyst attention picked up in early-to-mid July, with Paradigm Capital naming Perimeter a healthcare Top Pick and Brookline Capital Markets initiating coverage with a Buy rating and a C$1.54 price target built largely around the pending CMS New Technology APC reimbursement decision expected by year-end 2026. Company-specific news flow has otherwise been quiet through late July and into August, with the next major catalyst likely to be Q2 2026 financial results (expected August/September, date not yet announced) followed by progress on the Medicare reimbursement pathway seen as key to broader hospital adoption economics.
